page: Microsoft Azure F8alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of compute-focused platforms. Hardware features include 32 MB of L3 cache, support for AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI vector extensions, and a bundled 944 GB local NVMe SSD. It does not include a discrete GPU accelerator.

In benchmark assessments, the F8alds_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-threaded performance driven by its 4.5 GHz clock speed. It ranks in the top decile for stress-ng single-core processing as well as single-threaded compression benchmarks, achieving 41.29 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.23 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. The system also registers strong prompt processing and top-tier text generation on lightweight 135M parameter language models. Multi-threaded execution, memory bandwidth, and synthetic database transactions score within the middle 50% baseline, corresponding directly to its 8-core density.

The hardware configuration exhibits strong resource efficiency for workloads that require dedicated processing power without excessive memory overhead. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external disk latency for high-frequency operations, though the 16.0 GB memory capacity limits its utility for large in-memory databases. The server is well suited for CPU-bound applications, continuous integration pipelines, batch data compression, and web serving.
description: The Microsoft Azure F8alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 cores from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 16.0 GB of RAM alongside 944 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. It incorporates AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI vector instruction sets and operates without discrete GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the F8alds_v7 exhibits top-tier single-threaded compute performance, particularly in stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and lightweight model token generation. Multi-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth align with mid-range industry baselines. Given its dedicated clock speed and low-latency local storage, the instance is effective for CPU-intensive workloads such as CI/CD compilation, batch data transformation, and dedicated web application hosting.
